title: Idempotent Multi-Tenant Escrow & Double-Entry Ledger API with HMAC Reconciliation
objective: Implement an enterprise-grade, multi-tenant financial escrow engine and double-entry bookkeeping ledger in Python/FastAPI using SQLite and HMAC-SHA256. The system must support atomic balance tracking, zero-sum double-entry ledger journals, Idempotency-Key request deduplication with payload hash conflict detection (HTTP 422), two-phase escrow holds (authorization, partial capture, void, and lazy temporal expiration), and HMAC-SHA256 authenticated administrative reconciliation with clock skew protection.
motivation: Financial platforms (Stripe, Modern Treasury, Escrow.com) require strict mathematical zero-sum ledger invariants, robust multi-tenant data isolation, and guaranteed exactly-once payment semantics to prevent double-spending and ledger inconsistencies under high-concurrency distributed traffic.
difficultyExplanation:
1. Double-Entry Zero-Sum Invariant: Every financial operation (transfers, hold authorizations, captures, releases) must write balanced debit/credit rows to the immutable ledger_entries table such that total net transaction sums strictly equal zero.
2. Strict Idempotency & Conflict Semantics: Implementing atomic request fingerprinting in SQLite where replaying identical requests returns cached responses while mutated payloads with reused keys return HTTP 422 Unprocessable Entity.
3. Escrow Hold Lifecycle & Lazy Expiration: Correctly separating total account balance from available balance across active, captured, voided, and temporally expired holds without financial race conditions.
4. HMAC Timestamp Authentication: Validating constant-time HMAC-SHA256 request signatures with strict 300-second timestamp drift windows.
environmentSummary: Python 3.11-slim container with FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pytest, HTTPX, SQLite3, and pre-configured Pydantic schema models in /app.
oracleStrategy: Reference implementation in solution/ providing SQLite transaction boundaries, double-entry ledger bookkeeping, Idempotency-Key storage with SHA-256 fingerprinting, escrow hold state machines, and HMAC reconciliation.
verificationStrategy:
The verifier runs test.sh executing multi-stage hidden pytest suites evaluating:
1. Account creation and balance initialization.
2. Idempotency replay caching and payload mutation conflict rejection (422).
3. Two-phase escrow hold, partial capture, settlement, and voiding.
4. Temporal hold auto-expiration and lazy available balance releases.
5. Global double-entry zero-sum mathematical invariants across all accounts.
6. HMAC-SHA256 signature verification and clock skew validation.
binarySuccessCondition: Passes 100% of all hidden test suites across all 6 financial invariant phases with full reward score >= 0.95.
partialScoreStrategy:
Monotone scoring breakdown:
- 15%: Account CRUD and balance initialization.
- 20%: Idempotency caching and payload hash conflict detection.
- 25%: Two-phase escrow hold, partial capture, and voiding.
- 15%: Temporal auto-expiration and lazy balance recalculation.
- 15%: Double-entry zero-sum mathematical invariants.
- 10%: HMAC signature validation and timestamp clock skew.
anticipatedExploits:
1. In-memory balance mutation: Verifier executes raw SQL sum queries across ledger_entries table.
2. Single-entry shortcuts: Verifier asserts exact pair-wise debits and credits across all transactions.
